bridge: Builds on W01 through W17. This capstone supplies a complete fictional review packet; provider labs remain optional additional evidence.
teaching:
An integrated assessment tests whether you can connect a symptom to a violated invariant and a repair that preserves ordinary use. Listing vulnerability names is weaker evidence than a reproducible authorised case with expected and actual decisions.

Use a written scope and minimise data collection. Group multiple symptoms under their root cause when they share a fix, but keep independent boundaries separate. Severity should reflect a supported failure scenario, affected data and prerequisites, not the dramatic appearance of a tool screenshot.

A remediation report includes a verification plan with both negative and positive cases. It also records what was not tested. For independent study, exchange reports with the other learner, who should be able to reproduce the reasoning from the supplied packet without access to secret data.
example:
Fictional note API packet
A owns n1; B owns n2; body max100 chars.
Observed: A GET n2 ->200 with B's body.
Observed: PATCH n1 accepts owner=B from request body.
Observed: note preview inserts body using innerHTML despite plain-text contract.
Observed: A GET n1 ->200; B GET n2 ->200.
Scope: analyse packet only; make no external requests.
explanation: The first observation is object-authorisation failure, the second protected-property assignment, and the third a text/markup boundary problem. The packet supports design findings without requiring attack execution. Existing valid owner reads are essential regression cases.
exercise: Write three findings from the packet. Each needs problem, exact evidence, plausible impact, root cause, minimal repair and positive/negative verification cases. Include a scope and untested-behaviour section.
solution: Fix owner-constrained lookups, an explicit writable-field allowlist and text-safe rendering. Test both owners' valid actions, cross-owner denial, protected-field rejection and literal marker rendering. Avoid claiming code execution from the packet alone without evidence.
challenge: Independently review a changed packet: ownership checks are fixed, but the export preview still uses innerHTML and bulk PATCH still accepts owner. State which original findings remain, identify the alternate paths and propose a regression matrix.
challenge_solution: The object-read finding can close only for verified paths. Rendering and protected-field issues remain in alternate paths. Include main/export views and single/bulk writes. A fix in the primary screen does not establish coverage of every entrypoint.
